header.name: Differential Geometry
header.description: This course will strive to serve as an elementary account of the theory of curves and surfaces in Euclidean 3-space. It will be delivered using the language of differential forms which will also be introduced. The choice of differential forms will help provide a more modern treatment and facilitate relatively easier descriptions of many details. The lead up shall consist of theory building in ℝ3 needed for understanding the classical hallmarks of differential geometry – Gaussian curvature, Theorema Egregium of Gauss, geodesics, and Gauss–Bonnet Theorem. This course is aimed at senior undergraduate and postgraduate students with an interest in learning some beautiful mathematical theory but also which can be potentially applied to diverse areas of Mathematics (geometric analysis), Physics (general relativity), Computer Science (machine learning) among others.
prerequisites_mandatory: MTH 240 (Real Analysis I) or MTH 203 (Multivariate Calculus)

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Multivariable Calculus and Differential Forms: Students will have an understanding of calculus of multivariable functions and smooth differential forms in Euclidean space, and on curves and surfaces in ℝ3. They can apply these learnings to understanding the calculus of smooth geometries.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Curves, Surfaces and Curvature: Students will understand a local geometric description of curves and surfaces. They will learn about their various geometric invariants, and be able to perform algebraic analysis for different curves and surfaces in ℝ3.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Intrinsic Geometry of Surfaces: Having learnt how to measure shapes of surfaces, students will learn about the intrinsic theory of surfaces. This enable them to answer questions like the shape of a surface with a prescribed Gaussian curvature.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Riemannian Geometry of Surfaces: Students will integrate their learnings about differential geometry of curves and surfaces in ℝ3 to understanding a geometric theory of surfaces which is independent of the Euclidean embedding.

lecture_topics: Calculus in Euclidean space: overview of multivariable calculus
Curves in ℝ3: plane and space curves
More on curves: Serret-Frenet equations using differential forms as Cartan’s structural equations
Surfaces in ℝ3 and calculus on surfaces: definition of surfaces
surfaces of revolution and ruled surfaces
calculus for differentiable functions on surfaces
tangent planes and tangent vectors on surfaces
Shape operators and invariants of surfaces: shape operator (Weingarten map)
normal, principal, Gaussian, and mean curvatures
Differential geometry of surfaces in ℝ3
six fundamental form equations of a surface (first structural, symmetry, Gauss and Peterson–Mainardi–Codazzi Equations)

resources.title: Barrett O’Neill, Elementary Differential Geometry, Revised Second Edition, 2006
Tristan Needham, Visual Differential Geometry and Forms, 2021
Michael Spivak, A Comprehensive Introduction to Differential Geometry, Volume Two, Third Edition, 1999
V. I. Arnold, Methods of Mathematical Physics, Second Edition, 1988, Chapter 7
